tn.quote: Opm. Oudere Terschellingers maken verschil tussen a: in [hs:t] hard en de tweetoppige vocaal a: in [hs<:'t] haard. … < > boven vocaal duidt tweetoppig accent aan. … § 381. tn.translation: Note. Older Terschellingers distinguish ɔ: in [hɔ:t] 'hard' from the two-peaked vowel ɔ̂: in [hɔ̂:t] 'hâld (holds)' [scan 'haard'; phonetic symbols scan-garbled]. … ^ over a vowel marks two-peaked accent. … § 381. In contrast to Dutch … in Terschelling Frisian the long-short correlation is primary. … § 397. … Since the two words mentioned are the only ones in which ɔ: and ɔ̂: are still different phonemes, and present-day dialect speakers no longer observe this difference, … we may conclude that ɔ: and ɔ̂:, insofar as they have not merged, are phonetic realisations of one phoneme.
tn.cite: Knop, G. 1954. De spraakkunst der Terschellinger dialecten. Met een levensbericht door J.H. Brouwer (ed.). Taalkundige Bijdragen van Noord en Zuid VI. Assen: Van Gorcum. XXVI + 270 pp. [Delpher digitisation of the Koninklijke Bibliotheek copy, online since 17-03-2026]

5518.idn: Name in the source: tikar; family in the source: per the Atlas linguistique du Cameroun, 'à la charnière du bantou du Grassfield, du bantou du Mbam et du bantou équatorial', to be linked to the 'noeud bantou' (Introduction §3)

tones: ton modulé non-bas descendant à bas (falling, ^)
ton modulé bas montant à non-bas (rising, v)
tn.quote: On relève en tikar des tons ponctuels cl des Ions modulés. … Au niveau phonétique, le tikar connaîl trois tons ponctuels: haut, moyen, bas. … Donc, au niveau morphotonologique, l'opposition trinairc haut/moycn/bas est réductible à une opposition binaire bas/non-bas. … Quant aux tons modulés, sur le plan phonétique, il y en a quatre: haut-bas, moyen bas, bas haut et bas-moyen. … sur le plan morphotonologique, il y a lieu de ne distinguer que deux Ions modulés, à savoir: un ton non-bas qui descend à un ton bas et un ton bas qui monte à un ton non-bas.
tn.translation: Tikar has level tones and contour tones. … At the phonetic level Tikar has three level tones: high, mid, low. … So at the morphotonological level the three-way high/mid/low opposition is reducible to a binary low/non-low opposition. … As for the contour tones, phonetically there are four: high-low, mid-low, low-high and low-mid. … at the morphotonological level only two contour tones need be distinguished, namely a non-low tone that falls to a low tone and a low tone that rises to a non-low tone.
tn.cite: Stanley, Carol. 1991. Description morpho-syntaxique de la langue tikar (parlée au Cameroun). Épinay-sur-Seine / Yaoundé: Société Internationale de Linguistique (SIL). 581 pp. ISBN 2-87751-003-4.
tn.locator: pp. 18-19, ch. 1 'Rappel phonologique', §1.3 'Système tonal'
tn.note: Phonetic high, mid, low reduce to low vs non-low (mid predictable by noun class); two contour tones, falling and rising, on about 3% of the lexicon; downdrift in high-low-high; stress not described. Checked against the source (tone consistency check round 3, 2026-09-24): tone-bearing unit unstated -> syllable (ch. 4 §cl. 2 (nasal resyllabification) (also 860, 7186, 7276); ch. 2 …); downstep unstated -> yes (p. 28 §1.8 'Phrase phonologique'; ch. 1 endnote p. 40).

corr.words: Si la nasale était syllabique, c’est-à-dire porteuse d'un ton, elle perdrait son ton. ... la première syllabe portera un ton haut et la deuxième (le suffixe)» un ton bas. ... un ton bas sur la deuxième syllabe du radical devient haut.
corr.loc: ch. 4 §cl. 2 (nasal resyllabification) (also 860, 7186, 7276); ch. 2 hypothétique irréalisable; ch. 3

5520.idn: Name in the source: Cambap; family in the source: Bantoid ('Cambap is a Bantoid language'; speakers recognize it as closer to Mambila, e.g. the Langa and Kabri varieties; Mambiloid region)

tn.quote: Cambap has three level tones, High (H), Mid (M) and Low (L). In citation forms one normally finds one tone per syllable; contours are also attested, though on monosyllables they are rare. Contours are readily analyzable as sequences of level tones. That all possible combinations of H, M, and L are attested on both monosyllabic and disyllabic words provides strong evidence for this analysis. … Tone functions both lexically and grammatically, and contours may also come about through the application of grammatical tone (discussed below).
tn.cite: Connell, Bruce. 2002. Aspects of the phonetics of Cambap. Studies in African Linguistics 31(1/2): 179-210. doi:10.32473/sal.v31i1.107350
tn.locator: p. 201, section 6.1 'Inventory, contrasts and functions'
tn.note: Three level tones, High, Mid and Low, one per syllable, all nine two-tone combinations attested; contours are sequences of levels, some from grammatical tone (imperative MHL); stress not discussed.

tn.quote: Vale has two unambiguous tone levels, which I label as High (H) and Low (L). … Hence, all four of the tone patterns typically expected in a two-tone system occur in Vale. … In this view, the “Superhigh” tone is actually a H tone raised via the phonetic process H-Raising … The non-automatic downstep results from the presence of a floating L tone. … If we accept this view, Vale has five underlying tone melodies: L, H, LH, HL, and HLH. … CVV syllables have two moras and the tone bearing unit (TBU) in Vale is the mora.
tn.cite: Olson, Kenneth S. 2024. A preliminary phonology of Vale. In Yaqian Huang, Nina Hagen Kaldhol, Jun Jie Lim, Sharon Rose & Anthony Struthers-Young (eds.), ACAL in SoCAL: Selected papers from the 53rd Annual Conference on African Linguistics, 455–474. tn.note: Two level tones, H and L, with the mora as tone-bearing unit; five underlying word melodies L, H, LH, HL, HLH, the last surfacing as HꜜH through a floating L and non-automatic downstep.

evidence_works.work: Freeouf 2014, Review of Barclay, A Grammar of Western Dani (MANUSYA: Journal of Humanities 17: 104-108)
evidence_works.detail: Book review of Barclay 2008 (A Grammar of Western Dani, Lincom). Reports that the grammar has no discussion of tone or of word/sentence stress, and that its only mention of word stress is a hedged footnote (Barclay 2008 p. 39) offering penultimate stress as a possible explanation of lengthened vowels in class 4 verbs. 106-107: "Neither in the phonological section nor anywhere else in the grammar is there any discussion of suprasegmental features such as tone, whether it is phonemically functional or not, nor of word or sentence stress.... The only mention of word stress is contained in one sentence in a larger footnote as a possible explanation of a lengthened vowel in one verb (''It could be explained by stress assignment to the penultimate syllable, a process which could have caused the lengthened vowels in the class 4 verbs'' (p. 39)." Secondhand and hedged: not a basis for coding; a pointer to check Barclay 2008 p. 39 directly.

tn.quote: Sur le plan linguistique, le xârâgurè appartient aux langues kanak du groupe Sud, tout comme l'ajië, le tîrî, le haméa et le xârâcùù. Ces langues ne sont pas tonales, contrairement aux langues parlées plus au nord ou plus au sud. Elles comportent toutes un nombre important de phonèmes, et une structure syllabique caractérisée par l'absence de consonnes finales, sauf dans des emprunts récents.
tn.translation: Linguistically, Xârâgurè belongs to the Kanak languages of the South group, just like Ajië, Tîrî, Haméa and Xârâcùù. These languages are not tonal, unlike the languages spoken further north or further south. They all have a large number of phonemes, and a syllable structure characterised by the absence of final consonants, except in recent loanwords.
tn.cite: Moyse-Faurie, Claire. 2020 [HAL deposit 2023, 'à paraître']. Dictionnaire xârâgurè-français. Lacito-CNRS. 156 pp. (1. Présentation; 2. Conventions d'écriture et phonologie; 3. Esquisse grammaticale; lexique). hal-04299485.

tn.quote: Le xwela présente deux tons phonologiques: ce sont le tonème H et le tonème B qui ont différentes réalisations. Le tonème H se réalise haut sur une syllabe à consonne sourde ou sur une syllabe constituée d‟une voyelle comme ci-après en (1) (1) a. kú [ku] mourir b. /é/ [é] PPS (3ième pers. Sing) Il est réalisé BH sur une syllabe à consonne obstruante voisée. c. /ìví/ [ìvĭ] enfant d. /ìzέ/ [ìzɛ] canari Le tonème B se réalise bas [-`] sur une syllabe constituée de n‟importe quelle consonne de la langue. … Le ton M est une réalisation du tonème /B/: f./òló/ [ōló] “proverbe” /ìnũ/ [ìnũ] “ chose”
tn.translation: Xwela has two phonological tones: the toneme H and the toneme B [low], which have different realisations. The toneme H is realised high on a syllable with a voiceless consonant or on a syllable consisting of a vowel, as in (1): a. kú 'to die', b. /é/ [é] 3sg subject pronoun. It is realised BH [low-high, rising] on a syllable with a voiced obstruent: c. /ìví/ [ìvĭ] 'child', d. /ìzέ/ [ìzɛ] 'water jar'. The toneme B is realised low on a syllable with any consonant of the language. … The M [mid] tone is a realisation of the toneme /B/: f. /òló/ [ōló] 'proverb', /ìnũ/ [ìnũ] 'thing'.
tn.cite: Djanato, Odilon K. Sindeté. 2012. L'expression du temps et de l'aspect en xwelagbe. Mémoire de maîtrise (Sciences du Langage et de la Communication, option Description linguistique), FLASH, Université d'Abomey-Calavi; dir. Coffi Sambiéni. 57 pp. (BU-UAC mémoire no. 365, année 2012-2013.)

tn.note: Two phonemic level tones, high and low; high surfaces as rising after a voiced obstruent onset and low can surface as mid. Nothing said on downstep or word stress.

tn.quote: Les neuf (09) hauteurs tonales inventoriées sont récapitulées dans ce tableau (Tab. 6). … Ces oppositions ont permis de déterminer les trois tons à valeur distinctive suivants: /H/, /B/, /BH/. … Elle montre que l’unité porteuse de ton en nuasúɛ est la more et non la syllabe. … nous assertons qu’en nuasúɛ les tons modulés sont des cas de bitonématisme. … Au regard de ce qui précède, on distingue deux tonèmes de base: le tonème haut (TH) et le tonème bas (TB) récapitulés dans le tableau (Tab. 7) ci-dessous.
tn.translation: The nine (09) tonal heights inventoried are summarised in this table (Tab. 6). … These oppositions have established the following three tones with distinctive value: /H/, /L/, /LH/. … It shows that the tone-bearing unit in Nuasúɛ is the mora and not the syllable. … we assert that in Nuasúɛ the contour tones are cases of bitonematism [sequences of two tones]. … In view of the foregoing, two basic tonemes are distinguished: the high toneme (TH) and the low toneme (TB), summarised in the table (Tab. 7) below.
tn.cite: Bebine (Bébiné), Adriel Josias. 2019. Description phonologique et morphosyntaxique du nuasúɛ (langue bantu A62A). Thèse de doctorat, Université de Yaoundé I. HAL tel-03866872.

tn.quote: In conclusion, Yoy has five phonologically distinctive tones serving to distinguish between lexical items. The five tones of Yoy include mid-leveled tone (tone 1), high-rising tone (tone 2), mid-rising tone (tone 3), mid-falling tone (tone 4), and low-falling creaky tone (tone 5). Please note that all categories of words in Yoy can carry all tones. … Checked syllables in Yoy can carry only tone 1 (mid-leveled tone), tone 2 (high-rising tone), and tone 5 (low-falling creaky).

tn.quote: E. T o n o l o g i e Dzâmba. Il y a quelques groupes de parlers dans l’extrême ouest de la région étudiée, entre la Ngiri et l’Ubangi, qui ont une tonologie entièrement différente. Comme elle est, dans cette région, l’apanage des parlers Dzâmba, nous l’avons dénommée: la tonologie Dzâmba. … b. Les préfixes nominaux y ont toujours le ton haut. … à. La tonologie possède des tons doubles courts qui n’ont qu’une valeur tonétique … e. Enfin on a l’impression que la distance entre les tons hauts et bas est moindre …
tn.translation: E. Dzamba tonology. There are a few groups of lects in the far west of the region studied, between the Ngiri and the Ubangi, which have an entirely different tonology. Since in this region it is the preserve of the Dzamba lects, we have named it the Dzamba tonology. ... b. Noun prefixes there always have high tone. ... d. The tonology has short double tones which have only a tonetic value ... e. Finally one has the impression that the distance between the high and low tones is smaller [than in any other lect of the region; this will have to be checked later with instruments].

5531.prule: Stress is fixed and falls on the root-initial (stem-initial) syllable of the word (Otieno 2013, attributing the statement to Kaplan 2007, which does not contain it; inflectional prefixes precede the stem).
5531.quote: Kaplan (2007) points out that Dhopadhola stress is fixed and falls on the root initial syllable of the word. The syllable structure of the language is (C) V (V) (C). … The stressed syllable is underlined; it falls on the stem initial syllable. Dhopadhola like Dholuo has two tones and both are active in the prosodic phonology of the language.
5531.loc: sec. 5.2.6 'An Optimality Theoretic Perception Grammar Hypotheses and Predictions' (L1 word-stress background), p. 135
5531.idn: Name in the source: Dhopadhola; family in the source: southern Luo language; Western Nilotic branch of the Nilo-Saharan language family

tn.quote: Dhopadhola has two underlying level tones (tonemes): High (H) and Low (L) according to Kaplan (2007). The only contour tones in Dhopadhola are falling tones (HL and H!H), and they only appear on a phonological phrase –final syllable and on syllables with long vowels. CVN syllables, (where N is a nasal) appear word internally, and other closed syllables appear only word finally. Neither kind of closed syllable can host a contour tone. … Under certain conditions, a high tone may spread rightward to an adjacent low-toned syllable.
tn.cite: Ayieko, Gerry Otieno. 2013. The perception and learnability of English prosodic phonology by Luo speakers: a cross-linguistic experimental study. PhD thesis, Makerere University, Kampala (January 2013). hdl:10570/2752.

tn.note: Two level tones, High and Low (after Kaplan 2007); falling HL and H!H contours only phrase-finally or on long vowels; H spreads rightward; stress fixed on the root-initial syllable.

5532.idn: Name in the source: aprô (parler aïzi-kwa); family in the source: Kwa language of Côte d'Ivoire per title and introduction; the author reviews the Kwa vs Kru (or isolate) classification of Aïzi and states it is unresolved ('nous n'avons pour l'heure aucune certitude')

tn.quote: Au niveau tonal, l’on ajoute un ton haut au suffixe. En effet, lorsque le ton de la dernière voyelle est [B], le suffixe porte alors un ton modulé [BH]. … Pour les noms terminés par un ton haut ou [H], il y a une confusion tonale entre le morphème du défini et celui du nom. … à défaut de passer d’un ton haut à un ton super haut (ce qui n’est pas compatible avec le registre tonal de la langue), on assiste au maintien du ton ponctuel, d’où [H + H] = [H] … lorsque le ton du nom est [B]. Dans le cas d’espèce, l’on note l’apparition d’un ton modulé [BH] sur la dernière voyelle du nom.
tn.translation: Tonally, a high tone is added to the [plural] suffix: when the tone of the last vowel is [L], the suffix carries a modulated [LH] tone. … For nouns ending in a high tone [H], the definite morpheme's tone merges with the noun's. … rather than going from a high tone to a super-high tone (which is not compatible with the tonal register of the language), the level tone is maintained, hence [H + H] = [H] … when the noun's tone is [L] … a modulated [LH] tone appears on the noun's last vowel.
tn.cite: Assanvo, Amoikon Dyhie. 2021. Morphologie nominale en aprô, parler aïzi-kwa. Studii de gramatică contrastivă / Studies in Contrastive Grammar 35: 6-18. DOI 10.5281/zenodo.6364635.
tn.locator: p. 10 §2 'Pluralisation' and p. 16 §3.1 'Noms terminés par un ton Haut' / §3.2 'Noms terminés par un ton Bas'; see also p. 14 §3
tn.note: Level tones high [H] and low [B/L]; a rising (modulated) LH arises when a suffixal or floating high joins a final low; a super-high is excluded by the tonal register; no inventory stated.

tn.quote: Chrambo has five phonetic pitches which can occur on syllables in isolation. These are high [á], low [à],17 falling [â], and rising [ǎ]. Mid tone is found in Chrambo, but as a result of downstep, rather than as an underlying tone. … Monosyllabic noun roots can have one of four patterns: H, L, LH, HL. … These patterns can also be distributed over two syllables so that each syllable is realized as a level tone but the word has a rising or falling pattern … Verbs can be grouped in one of two tone patterns, High and Low.

tn.quote: Nous avons relevé trois niveaux de tons lexicalement distinctifs en banka, notés v̀ (bas), v̄ (moyen) et v́ (haut) respectivement. A part ce constat très fondamental, le système tonal de ce parler reste à étudier. L’assignation des tons lexicaux reste préliminaire, au moins pour une partie de nos données. Dans certains cas, nous avons même dû renoncer à une notation de tons, à défaut d’une hypothèse intitiale.
tn.translation: We recorded three lexically distinctive tone levels in Banka, written v̀ (low), v̄ (mid) and v́ (high) respectively. Apart from this very basic finding, the tonal system of this variety remains to be studied. The assignment of lexical tones remains preliminary, at least for part of our data. In some cases we even had to give up marking tone, for want of an initial hypothesis.

tn.quote: 2. 5. Tones Numbering of tones follows historical categories: 1 = A1, 2 = A2, 3 = B1, 4 = B2 C2 D2, 5 = C1, 7 = D1. Tone 2 is often breathy. tn.quote: 以、为前缀的双音节和四音节词，在 3187 个词中分别有 219 条和 249 条，多为名词。 选择还是作为前缀，主要依据是后一音节元音的舌位。后一音节元音为舌面前元音时，往 往与前缀搭配；后一音节元音为舌面后元音或舌尖元音时，多与前缀搭配。和音节还有 有高平、中平和低降调三个声调。声调的选择也与后一音节的声调高低相关。后一音节声调 高，前缀也多为高平或中平调；后一音节声调低，前缀则多为低降或中平调。
tn.translation: Disyllabic and quadrisyllabic words with the prefixes [a-] and [second vocalic prefix] number 219 and 249 of the 3187 words, mostly nouns. Which prefix is chosen depends mainly on the tongue position of the next syllable's vowel: a front vowel usually takes [a-]; a back or apical vowel mostly takes [the other]. The [a] and [other] syllables further have three tones: high level, mid level and low falling. Tone choice also correlates with the next syllable's tone: when it is high the prefix is mostly high or mid level; when it is low the prefix is mostly low falling or mid level.
tn.cite: 经典 (Jīng Diǎn). 2020. 碧约哈尼语双音节化的类型及产生机制 [Types and Generation Mechanism of Disyllabic Words in Biyo Hani]. 民族语文 Minzu Yuwen 2020(1): 76-82.

tn.quote: Chiru, like other Tibeto-Burman languages, is a tonal language. For the present study, the data was recorded from native speakers of Chiru. The recorded data was analysed using praat.exe.
